key_insight: Self-powered microsystems are moving from single-source harvesters to hybrid energy platforms, where materials advances must be matched by robust power management and integration.
engineering_relevance: For IoT, wearables, and cyber-physical devices, the main challenge is not only harvesting ambient energy but delivering stable, usable power under real-world conditions.
method: Reviews triboelectric, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor photovoltaic, and RF rectenna technologies
Highlights hybrid multi-source integration and system-level power management constraints
Surveys recent advances such as liquid-solid TENGs, broadband piezoelectric designs, and metamaterial RF harvesters
evidence_signal: The abstract cites specific performance gains such as over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved RF harvesting via metamaterial architectures.
watch_item: A key implementation risk is that ultra-low-voltage cold-start PMICs and storage degradation can limit practical deployment even when harvesting materials perform well.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
